chunks: And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id) from Muhammad ibn Sinan who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the one whom a person reaches, [meaning the standing at Arafah], so he has reached Hajj. He said: 'If he arrives at Jam' (Muzdalifah) while the people are at Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram before the sunrise, he has reached Hajj and his Umrah is not valid. And if he reaches Jam' after the sunrise, it is a separate Umrah and he has not performed Hajj. So if he wishes to stay in Mecca, he stays; and if he wishes to return to his family, he returns, and Hajj is still incumbent upon him.'
And it has previously passed in these narrations that whoever reaches Al-Mash'ar after the sunrise has missed Hajj, and this is also confirmed by what he narrated:

key_terms.أَدْرَكَ: Adraka, to reach or attain (in the context of performing a ritual at its prescribed time).
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ: Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram, specifically referring to the sacred monument at Muzdalifah.
key_terms.جَمْع: Jam' (Muzdalifah), the place where pilgrims collect stones and stay after leaving Arafah.
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: Sunrise, the critical time marker for determining the validity of the Hajj ritual.
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ: Umrah Munfradah, a standalone Umrah performed independently of Hajj.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim misses Arafah but reaches Muzdalifah before or after sunrise?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the critical distinction between the validity of Hajj and Umrah based on the timing of arrival at Muzdalifah (Jam') relative to sunrise. It establishes that arriving before sunrise validates the Hajj but voids the Umrah, whereas arriving after sunrise results in a missed Hajj (requiring repetition) while counting the stay as a standalone Umrah. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise temporal boundaries of ritual pillars, linking the physical act of standing to the spiritual validity of the pilgrimage.
